correctness.rationale: A complete border/marker classification proves exactly which zero-, one-, and two-marker factors are closed. Their distinct count is n+max(A,B)(min(A,B)+1). The bound and all optimizer triples follow from the exact integer optimization p+2q≤n−2; a direct independent closed-factor enumerator checks 680 full sets and the optimizer arithmetic through n=100. A compact simplex integral supports the average n²/36+O(n). Boundary n=2 and one/zero markers were checked; finite evidence supplements, not replaces, proof.

value.rationale: The 2013 general quadratic result uses marker blocks that grow with length; this exact theorem proves that just two occurrences of the minority symbol already support quadratic distinct closed-factor complexity, whereas fewer than two give exactly linear complexity. It provides an all-length sharp constrained maximum, all optimizers, a full factor characterization and a natural limiting mean. This is a structural sparsity threshold motivated by the core extremal complexity problem, not a narrow arbitrary table.
